claims.hypothesis: The high-frequency drop of the excess microwave emission (EME) in rho Oph W between 36 and 44 GHz follows a steep power law and varies across the PDR filament.
claims.experiment: Extracted intra-band spectra in the uv-plane by cross-correlating ALMA Band 1 visibilities with the pure-chi2 gpu-uvmem deconvolved model template over the whole mosaic and sub-regions.
claims.result: Measured an overall spectral index alpha = -0.78 +/- 0.05, varying from alpha_d = -0.16 +/- 0.14 in fields 5-6 (south-east) to alpha_d = -1.06 +/- 0.08 in fields 7-10 (north-west).
claims.finding: The EME spectrum in Band 1 is a power law with significant spatial variations in spectral index along the filament.

evidence.quote: It follows a spectral index $\alpha = -0.78\pm0.05$, in frequency, with some variations along the filament.

evidence.loc: Extraction of the intra-band diffuse emission spectrum
evidence.quote: The spectral index variations are very significant along the filament, from $\alpha_d = -0.16\pm0.14$ in fields 5 and 6 (south-east of the filament), to $\alpha_d = -1.06\pm0.08$ in fields 7 to 10 (north-west of the filament).

claims.hypothesis: Quasi-symmetric planar PAHs with permanent dipoles produce detectable evenly spaced rotational frequency combs in the Band 1 EME spectrum.
claims.experiment: Applied a matched-filter comb projection to the rectified cross-correlation spectrum across all 4 spectral windows for comb spacings from twice the channel width up to 200 MHz.
claims.result: No significant comb power was detected, with S(delta b)/sigma < 3.5 across ~2000 spacing values and < 3 x 0.06 of flux density in ~200 MHz combs.
claims.finding: There is no detectable comb-like fine structure in the Band 1 EME spectrum, likely because a large number of isomer configurations, non-planar geometries, and defect sites superimpose too many weak lines.

evidence.quote: There is no significant power in comb functions, with a spectral resolution as fine as twice the channel width: $\mathcal{S}(\delta b)/\sigma(\mathcal{S}(\delta b)) < 3.5$ in $\sim$2000 values for $\Delta \nu_{\rm line}$.
All these effects lead to the conclusion that there are so many weak lines superimposed that spectral structure cannot be detected, at least within the present limits (Fig. 11).

claims.hypothesis: The EME morphology in rho Oph W tightly follows the IR PAH emission morphology down to small angular scales.
claims.experiment: Cross-correlated Band 1 visibilities with star-subtracted Spitzer-IRAC templates as a function of uv-radius and compared high-resolution gpu-uvmem Band 1 images with IRAC and Herschel maps.
claims.result: The Band 1 to IRAC 3.6 um slope increases by a factor of 1.77 +/- 0.01 from short baselines to 7818 lambda (~20'' vs ~100''), Pearson r drops strongly with baseline length, and a compact (<7'') EME peak of 0.576 +/- 0.005 mJy/beam has no NIR or FIR counterpart.
claims.finding: The radio-IR correlation breaks down at small scales within the filament, with Band 1 showing a factor of ~2 enhanced power at high spatial frequencies and radio-only structures including a compact pure EME source.

evidence.quote: Relative to the IRAC power-spectrum, there is thus almost a factor of two more power in Band 1 at $\sim 20\ensuremath{''}$ than at $\sim 100\,\ensuremath{''}$.

As shown in Fig. 7b, the $r$ coefficients decrease strongly with baseline, which we attribute to the radio-IR correlation break-down when resolving the EME sources, even within the $\rho$ Oph W filament (see also Sect. 3.4 below).

evidence.loc: A compact EME source with no IR counterpart
evidence.quote: The compact EME source is smaller than the $\sim 7\ensuremath{''}$ beam, and bears no counterpart in the IRAC bands.

claims.hypothesis: Carbon radio recombination lines (C56alpha to C53alpha) from the C II PDR region should be detectable at LTE intensities of ~2 mJy/beam.
claims.experiment: Stacked the four CRRLs (C56alpha to C53alpha) present in the Band 1 correlator setup in a joint image.
claims.result: Non-detection with an upper limit of 0.15 mJy/beam in an 8.81'' x 6.53'' beam.
claims.finding: CRRLs are undetected at levels well below simple LTE predictions, possibly because collisional de-excitation in denser regions creates an unstructured emission map that is filtered out by the interferometer.

evidence.quote: We stacked all four lines in a joint imaging and obtained a limit of 0.15 mJy beam$^{-1}$, with a $8.81\ensuremath{''} \times 6.53\ensuremath{''}$ beam.

The non-detection of CRRLs is surprising and might be due to collisional de-excitation of the denser regions in the filament, resulting in an unstructured map, which might have beeen filtered out in the interferometer observations.

why_this_data.value: ALMA Band 1 (35-50 GHz) with ~39 antennas provides twice finer angular resolution (~7'') and much higher fidelity than the 5-antenna ATCA 39 GHz data, allowing imaging without an IR prior, clean removal of contaminating point sources like SR 4, and a search for spectral fine structure and CRRLs.

evidence.quote: The commissioning of the Band 1 receivers on the Atacama Large Millimetre Array (ALMA), covering 35 GHz to 50 GHz, offers the opportunity to map the filament with much better fidelity than with ATCA, and at finer angular resolutions.
The same ALMA observations can be used to search for fine structure in the EME spectrum, which may be used to identify its carriers (cite: Ali-Haimoud2014; Ali-Haimoud2015MNRAS.447..315A).

why_this_method.value: Visibility-plane cross-correlation with a pure-chi2 (lambda=0) gpu-uvmem model template avoids aperture photometry on faint single-channel diffuse emission, avoids negative bowls seen in CLEAN, and avoids the spectral index bias introduced by entropy regularisation (lambda=0.1) or differing IR template morphologies.

evidence.loc: Extraction of the intra-band diffuse emission spectrum
evidence.quote: The diffuse emission from $\rho$ Oph W is too faint for the extraction of its spectrum in individual channels through aperture photometry.

evidence.loc: Extraction of the intra-band diffuse emission spectrum
evidence.quote: It does, however, become detectable with the introduction of entropy, which is the reason we avoided regularisation.
In contrast, `gpu-uvmem` naturally suppresses large-scale negative artefacts, leading to a more physically plausible reconstruction in low-signal regions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Entropy regularisation (lambda = 0.1) in gpu-uvmem was tested and gave thermal residuals, but was rejected for spectral extraction because it introduced a significant bias in the derived spectral index (e.g. alpha = -0.26 +/- 0.09 on flat-spectrum simulations).

evidence.quote: However, with entropy regularisation, the spectral extraction technique turned out to be significantly biased (see Appendix 5).
We therefore opted to set $\lambda=0$ and truncated the optimisation at ten iterations to avoid excessive clumping.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Self-calibration (phase-only gaincal/applycal) was tested on individual execution blocks but rejected as unnecessary because S/N did not improve (101.81 vs 101.96).

evidence.quote: For comparison, before self-calibration the same restoration yields essentially the same value, with a somewhat larger S/N=101.96.
We concluded that self-calibration was not necessary for this dataset.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using Spitzer-IRAC maps directly as templates to extract the Band 1 spectral index was rejected because the Band 1 and IRAC morphologies/power spectra differ as a function of uv-radius.

evidence.quote: This confirms that the Band 1 and IRAC morphologies are appreciably different, and limits the use of the IRAC bands as templates to estimate the spectral index of the Band 1 signal, since varying frequencies correspond to varying $uv$-radii.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Multi-scale CASA-tclean was compared against gpu-uvmem and showed large-scale negative bowls and lower dynamic range.

evidence.quote: As explained in Appendix 6, after point-source subtraction `gpu-uvmem` generates images with much higher dynamic range than achievable with CASA-`tclean`.

However, on the largest angular scales the CLEAN image exhibits negative bowls, reflecting the limited ability of CLEAN to recover smoothly distributed emission in the presence of incomplete short-spacing coverage.

limitations_admitted.value: Severe interferometric flux loss (~70% missing flux; only ~29-30% recovered over the whole mosaic) due to missing short spacings in the 12 m array data.

evidence.quote: As described in Appendix 5, the flux recovered over the whole mosaic is $\sim$30%.

limitations_admitted.value: Resolved gradients in physical conditions and SEDs on the ~7'' synthesised beam scale cannot be constrained without 7 m (ACA) data; SEDs and spectral indices can only be reliably extracted on primary-beam scales.

evidence.quote: The present ALMA data cannot, however, be used to constrain resolved gradients in physical conditions across the PDR.
The combination of 7 m (ALMA Compact Array) observations with the present 12 m observations could allow for such a resolved multi-frequency analysis.

limitations_admitted.value: Pure-chi2 imaging (lambda=0) fits noise to some extent, creating positive-definite noise in the template that slightly biases the normalisation slope downwards (a_nu0 = 0.96 +/- 0.005).

evidence.loc: Extraction of the intra-band diffuse emission spectrum

limitations_admitted.value: The Airy-disk approximation to the ALMA Band 1 primary beam causes imperfect single-field point-source subtraction (~5% residuals) for the bright off-axis source DoAr 21, requiring a 4-field joint fit.

evidence.quote: We attribute the imperfect point-source subtraction for DoAr 21 in single-field point-source fits (with $\lesssim 5\%$ residuals) to the accuracy of the Airy disk approximation to the ALMA primary beam.

referee_caveats_inferred: Flux-loss correction relies on the IRAC 3.6 um template power spectrum matching the Band 1 EME power spectrum, even though the paper demonstrates that the two power spectra diverge by a factor of ~2 between ~100'' and ~20'' scales.

Truncation of unregularised (lambda=0) gpu-uvmem optimisation at exactly 10 iterations is an ad-hoc regularisation choice whose sensitivity on the small-scale clumping and spectral index is not systematically explored.
